Definition: Overall height, width and bounding dimensions
Pairing and correspondence of opposite holes
Wear, polish, grooving or abrasion on the knobs and knob necks, as distinct from wear on faces or inside the openings
Microscopic wear analysis distinguishing contact inside the bore of an opening from contact on its outer lip, as against the macroscopic impression recorded by EV017 and EV018

Whether every aperture on a single specimen can be told apart from every other, by diameter or by the number of concentric rings engraved around it. Distinct from EV004, which records the distribution of diameters, and from EV039, which records whether diameters conform to a standard between objects

Condition of the internal surface: whether it is smoothed or left as cast, and whether it carries any engraving, scale or marking. Distinct from EV012, which records casting quality overall, and EV014, which records decoration of the exterior

How hard the object actually was to produce: the failure rate of lost-wax casting at this geometry, the skill demanded, and the presence or absence of moulds, casting waste, rejects or workshop debris anywhere in the record

Whether the object carries a visual marking that singles out one axis or one face, as distinct from a structural feature such as a base or suspension loop. Distinct from EV038, which asks whether the FUNCTION requires a fixed orientation, and from EV014, which records the presence of decoration

Security of a specimen as an authentic ancient object: whether it has an excavated findspot, a documented collection history, and any metallurgical or technical authentication. Also whether it may be an ANCIENT local imitation of a classic type, as distinct from a modern forgery

Whether specimens of a single Greiner/Guggenberger type are more uniform in overall diameter, aperture set and wall thickness than the pooled corpus. Distinct from EV039, which measures standardisation across the corpus as one population and cannot detect type-mixing
